_trace.why: The diff computes nestingLevel via Math.max(8, ...others.map(...)) but the map's condition `i < placeholderGroups[idx].length` compares an others-array index to a length in a way that doesn't correlate with per-snippet tabstop counts, and it returns fixed 8 in nearly all branches rather than the actual number of tabstops in each nested snippet — so nestingLevel is effectively always 10 (8+2), not scaled to how many snippets/tabstops are merged, meaning the claimed fix for >10-tabstop (e.g. 16-tabstop 4x4 matrix) snippets doesn't actually happen. The final reindexing loop also unconditionally sets every non-final placeholder's index to i+1 based on group position, which discards the fractional nesting info entirely rather than 'reordering to avoid floating point problems' in a targeted way, and does not address the floating-point issue for >14 snippets as the description itself admits.
